olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Juan writes pairs $(n,3^n)$ and underlines them when $n$ and $3^n$ have the same units digit. What is the 2013th underlined pair?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $P_1,\ldots,P_{2013}$ sit at a round table with 10000 coins total. Starting with $P_1$: if even coins, give all to left neighbor; if odd, give an odd amount (at least 1, at most all) to left, keep rest. Prove eventually one person has all the coins.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Convex quadrilateral $ABCD$; $M$ = midpoint of $AB$. Circle through $D$ tangent to $AB$ at $A$ meets $DM$ at $E$. Circle through $C$ tangent to $AB$ at $B$ meets $CM$ at $F$. If $AF\cap BE$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, prove $A,E,C$ are collinear iff $B,F,D$ are collinear.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Ana and Beatriz alternate on a grid game starting with a $1\times 1$ square. Each turn: add a square sharing a full side with the current figure. A player wins if the figure becomes a rectangle with area divisible by 5. If Ana goes first, does either player have a winning strategy?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$ with circumcircle $\Gamma$; bisector of $\angle A$ meets $BC$ at $D$, $\Gamma$ at $K$, and tangent from $B$ at $X$. Show $K$ is the midpoint of $AX$ iff $\dfrac{DC}{AD}=\sqrt{2}$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all pairs of non-constant polynomials $p(x),q(x)$ with leading coefficient 1, degree $n$, and $n$ nonneg­ative integer roots, satisfying $p(x)-q(x)=1$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2013
